_aide: Traductions anglaises superposées au graphe français (clés = ids du graphe). Champs d'arête : theorem, statement, counterexample, strictnessExample. Champs de nœud : label, property (le \\text{...} du LaTeX est à traduire aussi). Ce qui manque reste en français et est signalé par generer_publications.py.

e1.statement: If \( f \) is continuous on \( [a, b] \), its image contains the whole interval \( [f(a), f(b)] \): for every value \( c \) between \( f(a) \) and \( f(b) \), there exists \( x \in [a, b] \) such that \( f(x) = c \).
e1.strictnessExample: x ↦ sin(1/x) (f(0) = 0) takes every intermediate value without being continuous at 0.

e25.theorem: A continuous function that is not monotone

e858.statement: Every element of « Parties de ℝ » is a subset of ℝ: this is the link between 𝒫(ℝ) and the real line itself. First orange edge (kind partie: A ⊆ 𝒫(B)).

e859.theorem: Inclusion in the collection of all sets
e859.statement: Every subset of ℝ is a set: the power set lives in the ambient collection.

C.label: Continuous real functions
C.property: \{\, f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \mid f \text{ continuous at every point of } \mathbb{R} \,\}

IVP.label: Darboux functions
IVP.property: \{\, f : f(I) \text{ is an interval for every interval } I \,\}

M.label: Monotone functions
M.property: \{\, f : f \text{ is nondecreasing on } \mathbb{R} \text{ or nonincreasing on } \mathbb{R} \,\}
